# Sources

The works this standard takes its terms from. Each is pinned by the SHA-256 of the bytes that were read; the bytes are
not part of this repository. `tools/standard.py fetch` puts them in a local cache, one file per source named by its
hash, and refuses bytes whose hash differs. A source is the work that introduced a term, a standard or specification,
official documentation, or a peer-reviewed reference work; openly edited wikis are not sources.

"Fetched from" is the address the bytes came from: a fixed version where one exists, otherwise the Internet Archive's
unmodified copy (`id_`) of the publisher's or author's address, or, marked in the note, an address whose bytes may
change. "Fragment" lands on the text relied on; where it is "—" the citation in the text gives a section or line.

The modules that describe a machine (x86-64, Apple arm64, RISC-V) add three more kinds of source: a vendor's
specification or manual; a measurement by a named measurer, cited together with the core it was taken on; and
source code at a pinned commit, cited as an exemplar. Module DOC adds a palette and a compiler, each at a fixed
version. A page that its publisher regenerates is pinned as the bytes read on the date shown, and its note says so.
